history.contribution:
**Reasoning about the missing pieces** When we sketch a campus‑wide waste‑sorting system it’s easy to jump straight to the hardware (bins, sensors, collection routes) and the software (data dashboards, reporting). What quickly becomes a blind spot, however, is **how the waste streams are actually defined** and **how we get people to use the system correctly**. If the categories are vague or overlap, users will be confused, contamination rates will sky‑rocket, and the data we collect will be meaningless. Conversely, if the engagement plan is just “post a few posters,” participation will be low and the system will never reach the validation milestones we need for a fast prototype. Below I flesh out two interlocking components that plug this gap: --- ## 1. Detailed Waste‑Stream Categorization | Primary Stream | Sub‑categories (what belongs) | Typical Bin Design (color/label) | Key Contamination Risks | |----------------|------------------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------| | **Recyclables – Paper & Cardboard** | • Office paper, flyers, newspaper
• Corrugated boxes, cereal boxes (flattened) | Blue, with “Paper & Cardboard – Flatten & Remove Plastics” | Food residue, plastic windows on boxes | | **Recyclables – Plastics & Metals** | • PET bottles, HDPE milk jugs
• Aluminum cans, steel food trays
• Rigid plastics #1‑#7 (clean) | Light‑green, “Plastics & Metals – Rinse & Empty” | Food‑soaked containers, mixed plastic/metal combos | | **Organic – Compostable** | • Fruit/veg scraps, coffee grounds
